countedThroughLabel: USSF-627 on Falcon 9, 12 Nov 2026 05:36 CET (04:36 UTC)
definition: All SpaceX launches in 2026 counted in UTC, including Starship flight tests (Flights 12 and 13 were suborbital; Flight 14 was the first orbital flight). This matches how SpaceX counts quarterly launches in its earnings materials.

quarterly.note: Company-reported totals (Falcon plus Starship flight tests). Q4 2026 is quarter-to-date from public launch logs, not a company figure.

starship.result: Suborbital test. Block 3 debut; 20 simulators and 2 modified Starlink V3 deployed. Booster lost in the Gulf, ship splashed down.
Suborbital test. First deployment of 20 Starlink V3 satellites (on a reentry trajectory, burned up as planned). Booster lost, ship splashed down.
First orbital Starship flight; deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, the first V3s in service.

milestones.title: Starship Flight 15
milestones.detail: First attempt to return and catch both Super Heavy and Starship at the launch site, and the first catch try for a V3 booster. 26 Starlink V3 satellites to orbit; about 14 orbits over a 22+ hour flight. Pending regulatory approval.

milestones.title: Starship Flight 16 — first from Florida
milestones.when: Tentative: mid-December 2026 per Florida reporting; other trackers list Q1 2027
milestones.detail: First Starship launch from LC-39A at Kennedy Space Center. Not yet confirmed by SpaceX.

milestones.title: Falcon 9 full-year target
milestones.detail: “Maybe 140, 145-ish” Falcon 9 launches in 2026. 120 flown through 12 Nov, so about 20–25 more would be needed in the last seven weeks.
